acceptance_criteria.criterion: API.getDialogues(slug, wpId) makes a GET /api/projects/{slug}/dialogues?wp={wpId} request.
API.getDialogueContent(slug, filename) makes a GET /api/projects/{slug}/dialogues/{filename} request.
The WP detail view includes a 'Dialogues' card rendered after the Handoff Notes card.
When no dialogues are returned, the card shows a 'no dialogues' message and no buttons.
When dialogues are returned, each filename appears as an interactive element labeled with its human-readable name (stage + revision, e.g. developer-r0).
Clicking a dialogue element fetches and renders the content as Markdown using marked.parse().
Clicking a second dialogue collapses the previously expanded one.
A fetch error shows an inline error message; it does not crash the rest of the WP view.
The Dialogues card does not appear above the Pipelines card in the rendered DOM.
All existing work-package.js rendering behavior is preserved (acceptance criteria list, pipeline badges, pipeline items, handoff notes still render correctly).

summary: Added API.getDialogues(slug, wpId) to api-client.js — makes GET /api/projects/{slug}/dialogues?wp={wpId}, returns parsed JSON.
Added API.getDialogueContent(slug, filename) to api-client.js — makes GET /api/projects/{slug}/dialogues/{filename}, returns raw text for Markdown rendering.
Added Dialogues card to renderWorkPackageDetail() in work-package.js — rendered asynchronously after Handoff Notes card via a #wp-dialogues-section placeholder.
Empty dialogues array shows a 'no dialogues' message with no buttons.
Non-empty array groups dialogues by stage; each stage shows revision buttons (r0, r1, …); latest revision has dialogue-btn-latest class (bold/blue highlight).
Clicking a button fetches content via getDialogueContent() and renders with marked.parse() in a scrollable .dialogue-content container.
Clicking a second button collapses the previously expanded one (activeBtn tracking pattern).
Fetch errors display an inline .text-danger message without affecting any other part of the WP view.
Dialogues card is injected after handoffHtml — therefore after Pipelines in DOM order.
All existing rendering (AC list, pipeline badges, pipeline items, handoff notes) is unchanged.
Added CSS for .dialogue-btn, .dialogue-btn-latest, .dialogue-btn-active, .dialogue-stage, .dialogue-content, .dialogue-markdown, and .text-danger utility class to styles.css.

comments.note: getDialogueContent uses a direct fetch() call rather than the private request() helper because request() calls res.json() but dialogue content is raw Markdown text. This is intentional and consistent with how getPlanDocument/getSynthesisDocument would need to work for raw content.

The #wp-dialogues-section placeholder div is injected synchronously into app.innerHTML so dialoguesEl reference is always valid before the async getDialogues() promise resolves, avoiding any race condition with view navigation.

Dialogue card is intentionally not rendered when the fetch returns an empty array — matching the spec ('If the array is empty, do not render the Dialogues card'). The empty-state message is shown only when the API call succeeds but returns zero items.

summary: All 10 acceptance criteria verified via code inspection and 22 automated jsdom tests written and passing.
Build check: node --check passes on api-client.js and work-package.js.
Regression: full test suite runs 1665 tests across 57 files — all pass, zero regressions.
AC1 verified: API.getDialogues makes GET /api/projects/{slug}/dialogues?wp={wpId}, URI-encodes slug and wpId, returns parsed JSON.
AC2 verified: API.getDialogueContent makes GET /api/projects/{slug}/dialogues/{filename}, returns raw text (not JSON), throws structured error on HTTP failure.
AC3 verified: #wp-dialogues-section placeholder injected synchronously after handoffHtml in app.innerHTML — Handoff Notes always precedes it in DOM order.
AC4 verified: empty array renders card with 'No dialogues available' message and zero buttons.
AC5 verified: buttons labeled stage-r{n}, latest revision gets dialogue-btn-latest class.
AC6 verified: click fetches content, calls marked.parse(), renders .dialogue-markdown wrapper.
AC7 verified: clicking a second button collapses first (activeBtn tracking pattern), same-button click is a toggle.
AC8 verified: getDialogues 500 error renders .text-danger in section without crashing WP view; getDialogueContent 403 renders inline error in content area.
AC9 verified: Pipelines card title precedes #wp-dialogues-section in DOM order.
AC10 verified: acceptance criteria list, pipeline badges, pipeline items, and handoff notes all render correctly with no regressions.
Edge case: null API response treated as empty (no crash). URI-encoding of special characters in slugs confirmed.

Implementation note: document.getElementById is used to locate the placeholder — app must be attached to the document for async callbacks to fire. This is correct browser behaviour. All production uses (the real SPA) attach to document, so this is not a defect.

metrics.test_coverage: All 10 ACs covered + 3 edge cases; 1665 total suite tests passing

comments.note: document.getElementById is used to locate the #wp-dialogues-section placeholder inside the async getDialogues callback. This requires app to be attached to the document when the promise resolves. In production (the real SPA), app is always the #app element in index.html, so this is never an issue. Test harnesses must attach the app element to document.body for the async path to execute.

getDialogueContent correctly uses a direct fetch() call (not the private request() helper) because it needs res.text() for raw Markdown rather than res.json(). This is consistent with how other raw-content endpoints would need to work and the deviation is intentional and documented by the Developer.
No dedicated test file existed for the dialogue feature prior to QA. Created tests/gui/dialogue-qa.test.ts with 22 tests covering all ACs and 3 edge cases. All pass.

summary: Code review PASS with one Fix-Forward applied. Three files reviewed: api-client.js (2 new API methods), views/work-package.js (Dialogues card rendering, async fetch, collapse toggle, error handling), styles.css (dialogue component styles). All 10 ACs satisfied. Architecture is sound and consistent with existing SPA patterns.

Fix-Forward applied: removed unused id='dlg-content-{stage}' attribute from .dialogue-content divs in work-package.js. The ID was generated via escapeHtml(stage) but never queried — content area is always retrieved via closest('.dialogue-stage').querySelector('.dialogue-content'). Dead attribute removed to prevent future maintainer confusion.

Documentation-Forward: getDialogues hand-rolls its query string ('?wp=' + encodeURIComponent(wpId)) instead of using the existing buildQueryString helper. Consistent with getRunLogEntries precedent (also hand-rolls its ?after= query string), but the pattern divergence from getProjects (which uses buildQueryString) is worth documenting for future API method authors.

Documentation-Forward: marked.parse() output is assigned directly via innerHTML — intentional and consistent with other Markdown rendering in the SPA, but worth noting in the component documentation that dialogue content is rendered as trusted HTML (no sanitization layer).

Documentation-Forward: dialogue-btn elements have no aria-expanded attribute to communicate toggle state to screen readers. A future accessibility pass should add aria-expanded toggling alongside the dialogue-btn-active class.

No blocking issues found. getDialogueContent correctly uses direct fetch() for res.text() (not the private request() helper which calls res.json()). Async placeholder pattern (synchronous innerHTML set, dialoguesEl captured by closure, then async resolution into the pre-captured reference) is correct and race-condition-free. Error paths are isolated and do not affect the rest of the WP view.

comments.note: Removed unused id='dlg-content-{stage}' from .dialogue-content div in work-package.js (line 202). The attribute was generated but the code always retrieves the content element via btn.closest('.dialogue-stage').querySelector('.dialogue-content') — never by ID. Removing it eliminates dead HTML and avoids confusing future maintainers who might try to use the ID as a selector. Non-behavioral change; QA validation remains valid.

getDialogues (api-client.js:63–65) hand-rolls its query string ('?wp=' + encodeURIComponent(wpId)) rather than using the internal buildQueryString helper. The deviation is intentional (single-parameter case) and consistent with getRunLogEntries, but diverges from getProjects which uses buildQueryString. Documentation should clarify the pattern decision for future API method authors.

marked.parse(md) output is set via innerHTML without a sanitization pass (work-package.js:257). This is consistent with the rest of the SPA's Markdown rendering and intentional for a local-network tool, but the component documentation should explicitly state that dialogue content is rendered as trusted HTML.

dialogue-btn toggle buttons have no aria-expanded attribute — screen readers cannot infer the expanded/collapsed state from the DOM. A future accessibility pass should add aria-expanded='false' initially and toggle it alongside the dialogue-btn-active class on click.

The activeBtn collapse pattern correctly handles three distinct cases: (1) first click — activate; (2) same-button click — toggle off; (3) different-button click — collapse previous, activate new. The guard order (activeBtn && activeBtn !== btn check before activeBtn === btn check) is correct.
